title: SDK integration walkthrough - Python + TypeScript quickstart
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript. Covered auth (API key vs SSO/service principals), environment setup, examples for chat/generate/embeddings, streaming, and a small plan for a short POC benchmark. Security questions (KMS, audit logs, VPC) flagged for follow-up.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick sdk walkthrough today. um so quick intro - i'm maya, AE at Redwood; with me is Liam, our SE.
[00:12] Elena Gomez: thanks maya, excited, we have rahul and samir here - quick note i'm pm for search.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: great, real quick agenda: install, auth, run a python quickstart, then a ts streaming example, then Q&A.
[00:30] Rahul Patel: sounds good, our main constraints are latency <200ms on critical flows and data residency in us-east-1, also curious about dedicated vs hosted.
[00:41] Maya Chen: noted, we'll show how to pin region and model variants; dedicated is an option if you need predictability.
[00:48] [00:48] (speaker overlap) Samir Khan: and we need to use our KMS for key wrapping, SAML is required for console access - security will ask.
[00:55] Liam O'Connor: yep we support KMS integrations and SSO; we'll share the SOC2 docs after.
[01:04] Maya Chen: ok install - Python: pip install redwood-sdk (note: pip package name in beta is redwood-inference in some regions, small mismatch in docs), TypeScript: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk.
[01:25] Liam O'Connor: env var is REDWOOD_API_KEY, simplest flow is: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx. For private deployments you can use a service principal and role-based tokens, and the console lets you create scoped API keys.
[01:42] Elena Gomez: can we use short-lived tokens via SSO?
[01:46] Liam O'Connor: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC will mint short lived creds; we can map groups to roles for RBAC.
[01:52] [02:00] (transcription glitch) Maya Chen: here's a python snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), region='us-east-1')
resp = client.chat.create(messages=[{"role":"user","content":"summarize latest merch KPIs"}])
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
[02:35] Rahul Patel: for embeddings, latency and tokenization are important, what models do you recommend?
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: for semantic search we recommend the redwood-embed-2 family, quantization profiles can reduce cost, we'll recommend config based on corpus size.
[02:52] Maya Chen: quick TypeScript demo: import {Redwood} from '@redwood-inference/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); const stream = client.chat.stream(...).
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: streaming is compatible with our hosted API and Dedicated; note that in some client libs the event names differ (we had previously named them "token" vs "delta" so you might see old examples).
[03:25] Samir Khan: any CORS considerations for embedding the widget?
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: yes, browser keys must be restricted and you should use a backend token exchange for anything privileged; we'll share a sample token-exchange lambda.
[03:40] Elena Gomez: how do we pin model versions for consistent outputs?
[03:44] Maya Chen: you can pin model version in the request or in a route config in the console; rollouts support canary and A/B via the console.
[03:53] Alex Ortiz (Security): on audit logs, retention, and encryption at rest - are logs sent to our SIEM?
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: we provide audit logs, and for Private deployments you can ship logs to your endpoint; for Hosted we can integrate with customer SIEMs via webhooks or syslog sinks on enterprise plans.
[04:14] Maya Chen: quick demo of the console: show API keys, create a scoped key (team-search) and restrict to model/embed endpoints. (link: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart - shared)
[04:36] [04:36] (brief screen-share pause)
[05:02] Rahul Patel: about the POC benchmark, can you run a small throughput test? we want 1k concurrent requests and a p99 under 200ms.
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: yes, we can run a dedicated benchmark - we'll need a sample workload, sequence length dist, and target model. we can do this in hosted sandbox or Dedicated trial.
[05:25] Maya Chen: next steps we'll share a starter repo with python + ts quickstarts, plus a benchmark spreadsheet template.
[05:33] [05:33] (crosstalk) Elena Gomez: great thanks.
[05:38] Maya Chen: any other questions?
[05:40] Jia Li: small one - do you have an example of caching prefixes?
[05:43] Liam O'Connor: yes, we have prefix caching in the client and at the route level; we'll send an example config.
[05:52] Maya Chen: ok i'll recap action items and we'll wrap.
[05:57] [06:00] (end of recording)
